big_case.notes: The stay could affect a parent's time with her child while state proceedings continued. The use of a parent's silence during a parallel prosecution raises a recurring federal question. This order resolved interim relief for one family and supplied no rule for other courts.

leakage.notes: Forward at arrival. The searches and fetches targeted linked petition 26-502, the Oklahoma proceedings, authorities and comparison dockets. Some requests sought the full linked docket. All 62 calls are outcome-only, so the log does not establish what the results contained. The retrieval note describes the linked petition's earlier sealing order and discloses a search-source listing without forecast content. Neither the rationale nor the log shows the November 19 stay disposition reaching the candidate.

central_claims.basis: The application was submitted November 16. The November 19 entry names Justice Gorsuch as denying the stay and granting leave to file the application and appendix under seal.
central_claims.claim: Justice Gorsuch would deny the stay himself in a brief order about three to ten days after submission and act on sealing at the same time.

central_claims.basis: Both response_requested and referred_to_court are false in the recorded interim signals.
central_claims.claim: Justice Gorsuch would act without requesting a response from Oklahoma or referring the stay to the full Court.

central_claims.basis: The November 19 disposition gives no legal ground and says nothing about § 1257 or the likelihood of certiorari.
central_claims.claim: The unresolved termination proceedings would make finality under § 1257 an obstacle to certiorari and a reason to deny on the papers.

central_claims.basis: The outcome counts zero amicus briefs. The docket records only Gorsuch's brief disposition and identifies no separate writing.
central_claims.claim: There would be no further amicus filings and no separate statement or dissent on the denial.
